steps: List all bonds broken in reactants — multiply each bond energy by the number of that bond type
List all bonds made in products — multiply each bond energy by the number of that bond type
ΔH = energy to break bonds − energy released making bonds
Negative ΔH = exothermic; positive ΔH = endothermic
method_card.title: Bond Energy Calculations
method_card.content:
Every bond energy calculation has two sections: bonds broken and bonds made.

Bonds broken — always endothermic (energy in). List each bond type in the reactants and multiply by its count.

Bonds made — always exothermic (energy out). List each bond type in the products and multiply by its count. Remember to multiply by coefficients in the balanced equation.

Overall: ΔH = energy in − energy out. Negative = exothermic; positive = endothermic.

Common pitfalls:

  • Not counting all bonds — in 2H₂O there are 4 O-H bonds total (not 2)
  • Getting the sign wrong — bond breaking is energy IN, bond making is energy OUT
  • Using the wrong bond type (C=O double bond has higher energy than C-O single bond)

exam_context.frequency: Medium — bond energy questions appear regularly

gold.display: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. Bond energies: N≡N = 945, H-H = 436, N-H = 391 kJ/mol. Calculate ΔH.

misconceptions.message: Bonds broken: N≡N (945) + 3×H-H (1308) = 2253 kJ. Bonds made: 2×NH3 = 6 N-H bonds = 6×391 = 2346 kJ. ΔH = 2253 − 2346 = −93 kJ/mol.
2NH3 has 6 N-H bonds total (3 per molecule × 2 molecules).

gold.display: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Bond energies: C-H = 412, O=O = 498, C=O = 743, O-H = 463 kJ/mol. Calculate ΔH.

misconceptions.message: Broken: 4×C-H (1648) + 2×O=O (996) = 2644. Made: 2×C=O (1486) + 4×O-H (1852) = wait: CO2 has 2 C=O bonds, 2×H2O has 4 O-H. Made = 2×743 + 4×463 = 1486+1852 = 3338. ΔH = 2644−3338 = −694. (Note: use values as given — answer depends on bond energies provided to the student.)
Bonds broken: CH4 has 4 C-H bonds. Each O2 has 1 O=O. Count all bonds carefully.

gold.display: A reaction has bonds broken = 1,200 kJ and ΔH = +300 kJ/mol. Calculate the energy released when bonds form in the products.

misconceptions.message: ΔH = energy in − energy out. 300 = 1200 − energy out. Energy out = 1200 − 300 = 900 kJ.

bronze.display: H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl. Bond energies: H-Cl = 432 kJ/mol. What is the total energy released making all bonds in the products (2 HCl molecules)?
bronze.equation_hint: Multiply bond energy by number of bonds made

bronze.display: Using your answers above (679 kJ in, 864 kJ out), calculate ΔH for H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl.

misconceptions.message: ΔH = 679 − 864 = −185 kJ/mol. The negative sign means exothermic.

bronze.equation_hint: Positive ΔH = endothermic; negative ΔH = exothermic

misconceptions.message: Positive ΔH means more energy was absorbed breaking bonds than released making bonds — endothermic.
